Metadata.homeDescription: Excellence AI is a secure enterprise MCP server that connects your team's AI tools to company systems — with governed access, a full audit trail, and human approval.
Metadata.privacyDescription: Privacy Policy for Excellence AI. How Excellence Pay Kft. accesses, collects, uses, stores, shares, protects, retains, and deletes personal data, including Google user data from Gmail and Google Drive.
Metadata.gtcDescription: General terms and conditions for Excellence AI, the enterprise MCP server operated by Excellence Pay Kft.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.description: This Privacy Policy explains how Excellence AI accesses, collects, uses, stores, shares, protects, retains, and deletes personal data — including Google user data from Gmail and Google Drive.

Terms.title: Terms of Service
Terms.description: The terms for using Excellence AI. The service is an invitation-only enterprise workspace, not a public consumer chatbot.

Home.badge: Enterprise MCP server · Operated in the EU
Home.heroBody: Excellence AI is an enterprise MCP server: the secure, standard connection between AI tools and company systems. Your team keeps its familiar tools; you control access, approvals, and the audit trail.
Home.featureMcpBody: No new chatbot to roll out. Your team keeps working in the AI tools they know, while Excellence AI connects them securely to company systems.
Home.featureAccessBody: You decide who can access each company system. Sensitive actions only run after a human approves them.
Home.featureAuditBody: Every AI action is logged: who asked for it, which data was accessed, and what happened. Everything can be reviewed later.
Home.featureAdminBody: Company administrators manage AI agents, system connections, roles, and autonomy. Only approved capabilities are available.
Home.featureModelsBody: Claude, Codex, ChatGPT, Gemini, or Grok — your team uses what works. Company governance always stays in Excellence AI.
Home.howStep1Body: Who can use each AI tool and company system, and which actions require human approval.
Home.howStep2Title: The team connects its AI tools
Home.howStep2Body: One secure company MCP address. Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, or any MCP-compatible client — the same connection.
Home.howStep3Title: A human decides at the sensitive points
Home.howStep3Body: File writes, folder creation, outbound actions: an approval card, one click.
Home.aboutBody: Excellence AI connects your team's AI tools to company systems. The company manages access, approvals, and audit in one place, while employees keep working in the tools they already know.
Home.aboutCardLead: <brand>Excellence AI</brand> is an enterprise MCP server operated by Excellence Pay Kft. It gives any MCP-compatible AI governed access to company systems — with a full audit trail, privacy safeguards, and human approval.
Home.aboutCardRest: The service is a closed, invitation-only enterprise workspace, not a public chatbot. External account connections are always optional; see the <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy> and <terms>Terms</terms> for details.
Home.ctaTitle: Every MCP-compatible AI. One control point.
Home.ctaBody: Sign in and connect your team's AI tools to company systems.
Home.termPrompt: Create a folder for the Q3 contracts

projects.title: Projects and project memory
projects.body: A project holds shared work files (plans, notes, drafts) and the teammates’ approved continuity knowledge: decisions, open tasks, findings. Pick a project and a teammate, then browse or edit memories.

skills.title: Skills
skills.body: A skill is a written workflow: it tells the AI teammate how to do a recurring job. On its own it cannot act — what it can actually do depends on the permissions given to the agent.
skills.hint: Every change starts as a proposal (proposed), and only becomes live (active) after approval — you can always roll back to an earlier version.
skills.migrateHint: If you just pulled new code, run the migration (npx prisma migrate deploy), then restart the dev server.
skills.needOperator: Viewing skills requires at least operator access.

knowledge.title: Knowledge base
knowledge.body: A shared document library: upload once, then attach it on an agent’s page to whoever needs it. Attachment copies the document — later catalog updates do not overwrite the copy on the agent.
knowledge.needOperator: Viewing the knowledge base requires at least operator access.
knowledge.loadFailed: The catalog could not be loaded.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.body: Append-only, hash-chained event log of the organization’s MCP and approval actions. Tokens and secrets are not stored in metadata.
audit.empty: This organization has no audit entries yet.

iam.title: Access
iam.body: Invites, roles, suspension, and lock-out protection in one place.

redeem.title: Activate access
redeem.body: The invitation token is single-use. After redeeming it, the account’s role becomes active.

settings.title: Workspace settings
settings.body: This workspace’s own behaviour. The Google OAuth client lives under Platform · Settings; menu visibility is on the Menu access page.
settings.languageBody: Skill descriptions and other human-readable text are written in this language. JSON keys stay in English.
settings.mcpIntroBody: This text appears in the MCP initialize instruction and in the platform.whoami response. Describe the company the AI is joining, and how it should treat published teammate agents.
settings.mcpIntroPlaceholder: Example: Ostorosbor Zrt. is a Hungarian winery. Teammates are published AI agents — CRM, sales, knowledge base.
settings.mcpIntroSaved: MCP introduction saved. AI clients will see it on the next connection.

menuAccess.title: Who sees which menu
menuAccess.body: Set which menu items and submenus each role sees in the header. By default everyone sees the full menu for their role — hide items that are not part of that role’s daily work.
menuAccess.help: A checkmark means that role sees the item in the header. Unchecking only removes it from the menu — the page’s access gate stays the same, so this is housekeeping, not an access restriction. If a role cannot reach a page anyway, that cell is not editable.
menuAccess.lockedTitle: This cannot be hidden from administrators — otherwise the menu could not be restored.
menuAccess.noAccessTitle: The {role} role cannot see this page because of its permissions.
menuAccess.savedEmpty: Saved. Every role sees the full menu allowed by its permissions.
menuAccess.saved: Saved. It applies to affected users from the next page load.

platformTenants.title: Workspaces
platformTenants.body: Customer (workspace) registry and lifecycle. Each workspace has its own agents, connectors, playbooks, and audit view — there is no data sharing between workspaces.
platformTenants.needPlatform: This screen requires platform-level access (superadmin / platform operator).
platformTenants.usersLoadFailed: The user list did not load — adding members and choosing the first admin is unavailable.

platformIam.title: Platform IAM
platformIam.body: Platform-level roles and the audit trail of workspace lifecycle / superadmin assume. A platform role is not a workspace role — a superadmin may enter workspace data only after an explicit, audited assume.

platformSettings.title: Settings
platformSettings.body: Clerk/OAuth, Google Drive, and Google Analytics / Search Console / Ads client settings. Model routing and budget have been removed.

GetStarted.title: Work in your favourite AI tool
GetStarted.body: Connect the platform to Codex, Cursor, Grok, Claude, or Goose. Pick your app and follow the short install steps.
GetStarted.step1Body: You can use the same server address in every app.
GetStarted.codexBody: Paste the command into the terminal. Browser sign-in opens; use the same account you are using here.
GetStarted.cursorBody: The button opens Cursor and offers to install the server. Then sign in in the browser.
GetStarted.cursorFallback: If the button does not work, you can add the MCP URL above by hand in Cursor settings.
GetStarted.grokBody: Paste the command into the terminal. On first connect, sign in in the browser with your platform account.
GetStarted.grokHint: In Grok you can also open sign-in via /mcps → server → i.
GetStarted.claudeDesc: Add a connector in the app
GetStarted.claudeBody: Open Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. For the name enter: {name}, for the URL paste:
GetStarted.claudeAfter: Then sign in with the same account you are using here.
GetStarted.claudeCodeBody: Paste the command into the terminal, then complete the sign-in Claude Code offers.
GetStarted.claudeCodeHint: This command is for Claude Code. For Claude Desktop use the guide above.
GetStarted.gooseDesc: Remote MCP extension in the app
GetStarted.gooseStep1: Open the Goose sidebar, then choose Extensions → Add custom extension.
GetStarted.gooseStep2: For type, choose the Streamable HTTP remote extension.
GetStarted.gooseStep3: For the id enter: {name}; for the name: Excellence AI. The server URL is:
GetStarted.gooseAfter: Click Add, then sign in with your platform account in the browser that opens.
GetStarted.step2Body: Open the connected AI tool and ask: “Who am I, and what AI teammates do I have?” If your teammates appear, the connection works.
GetStarted.reopenHint: You can reopen this page from the header at any time.
